baslik_tr: UAEA Başkanı Grossi BM Genel Sekreterliğine Aday Oldu
ozet_tr: Uluslararası Atom Enerjisi Ajansı Başkanı Rafael Grossi, Birleşmiş Milletler genel sekreterliği için adaylığını koydu. Al Jazeera sitesinde yayımlanan analize göre Grossi, ABD Başkanı Donald Trump ve Arjantin Başkanı Javier Milei ile kurduğu yakın ilişkiler nedeniyle eleştiriliyor. Yazara göre Grossi'nin önerdiği reformlar, bu iki liderin gündemiyle örtüşüyor ve ajansın bağımsızlığına dair soru işaretleri yaratıyor. Yarışta çekilen adayların ardından sekiz isim yarışırken, öne çıkan diğer aday BM Ticaret ve Kalkınma Konferansı başkanı Rebeca Grynspan oldu. Yazı, Grossi'nin olası liderliğinin küresel teşkilatın siyasi yönünü nasıl etkileyeceğini tartışıyor.
baslik_orj: International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) chief Rafael Grossi is seeking to become the next UN secretary-general, but his close ties to US P…
baslik_en: IAEA Chief Grossi Runs for UN Secretary-General
ozet_en: International Atomic Energy Agency Director General Rafael Grossi has put forward his candidacy for United Nations secretary-general. According to an analysis published on the Al Jazeera website, Grossi faces criticism over his close relations with US President Donald Trump and Argentine President Javier Milei. The author notes that the reforms proposed by Grossi align with the agendas of these two leaders, raising questions about the agency's independence. With several candidates having withdrawn, eight contenders remain in the race, with Rebeca Grynspan, head of the UN Conference on Trade and Development, emerging as another prominent figure. The article discusses how Grossi's potential leadership could affect the political direction of the global organization.

baslik_en: Human Rights Organizations Call for White Phosphorus Action
ozet_en: Eleven human rights and non-governmental organizations, including Human Rights Watch and Amnesty International, called on governments to strengthen international restrictions. The organizations issued a joint statement citing the use of incendiary weapons such as white phosphorus in densely populated areas in the Gaza Strip and southern Lebanon since October 2023. Human Rights Watch verified twenty-three incidents of Israeli forces using white phosphorus in southern Lebanon between March and May 2026. These incidents included airbursts over residential areas that were indiscriminate in nature and violated international humanitarian law.

Al-Hayya stated that despite the Palestinian resistance approving the outcomes of the Sharm el-Sheikh agreement, the occupation continues its attacks on the Gaza Strip. Emphasizing that the people view resistance as the only option to reclaim their land and sanctities, al-Hayya noted that the enemy has not limited itself to Palestine but has also attacked Lebanon, Syria, Iraq, and Iran. Stating that Israel has moved to implement the "Greater Israel" project, al-Hayya expressed determination to continue the resistance and activate its role in the region.

baslik_en: UN General Assembly Affirms Palestine's Right to Independence
ozet_en: The United Nations General Assembly approved a draft resolution affirming the Palestinian people's right to self-determination and independence. Submitted by the Third Committee dealing with human rights and humanitarian issues, the draft was adopted with 162 votes in favor and 8 against. Turkey, European Union members, Canada, Australia, and the majority of countries in Asia, Africa, and South America voted in favor, while the US, Israel, Argentina, Paraguay, Micronesia, Nauru, Papua New Guinea, and Palau voted against. The adopted resolution underscores the Palestinian people's right to live freely and independently on their own land, away from Israeli occupation.

baslik_en: Draft Resolution on Palestinian Independence Adopted at the UN
ozet_en: A draft resolution affirming the Palestinian people's right to self-determination and independence was voted on in the UN General Assembly's Third Committee. In the vote, 162 countries voted in favor, 8 voted against, and 8 abstained. The US, Israel, Argentina, Paraguay, Micronesia, Nauru, Papua New Guinea, and Palau voted against, while Cameroon, Colombia, Ecuador, Fiji, the Marshall Islands, Panama, Samoa, and Togo abstained. The Egyptian representative emphasized the urgency of ending the occupation, while the Israeli representative argued that the decision does not advance peace. The US representative stated that politicized resolutions undermine peace efforts, and the Tunisian spokesperson drew attention to the conditions of the people living in tents.
